citations.quote: But how do we measure default and equity risk? More importantly, how do we come up with the default and equity risk premiums?
Studies such as Banz (1981) and Keim (1983) have consistently found that smaller firms (in terms of market value of equity) earn higher returns than larger firms of equivalent risk
Stocks selling for well below the book value of equity have generally been considered undervalued, while those selling for more than book value have been targeted as overvalued.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Fama-French extends CAPM with two portfolio-constructed factors at security level: HML (high-minus-low book-to-market, value) and SMB (small-minus-big market cap, size). Each factor is a long-short portfolio return series; a security's exposure is its beta in a multivariate regression. Damodaran's market-efficiency evidence motivates the extension.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Fama-French Construction at Security Level
